summary.headline: Aditya Infotech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore with EBITDA margin of 18%; FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore, with EBITDA up 162% to INR258.3 crore and margin up 800 bps to 18%, helped by price rise, low-cost inventory and SKU mix. Full-year FY26 revenue reached INR4,220.8 crore (+35.6%), EBITDA INR579 crore (13.7% margin) and adjusted PAT INR368 crore (+166.1%). Management raised FY27 guidance to revenue INR6,000-6,500 crore, EBITDA margin 14-15% and PAT margin 8.5-9.5%. Management flagged that low-cost inventory is now exhausted and component costs (chips, memory, USD, freight) will keep rising through 2027, so price increases are being passed on monthly in small steps.

financial_highlights.change: Debt repaid from IPO proceeds; Q4 finance cost down 38%

segments.name: CP PLUS brand
segments.commentary: Contributed 86% of AIL revenue in Q4 and FY26; IP products are 73% of the CP PLUS portfolio.

segments.name: Camera/CCTV (India market)
segments.commentary: Company market share about 45.4% as of Q3 FY26, versus about 30% overall and about 25% for CP PLUS at the start of the journey. Management says it is not targeting a specific share number.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore, about 50% growth over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 14-15%; PAT margin around 8.5-9.5%. Management called 14-15% the new normal for FY27 and FY28, with Q4 a one-off above that level.
Unit volume growth target 25-30%, against an industry CCTV unit growth estimate of 15-16%.
Average per-unit camera realisation expected to rise 20-25% in FY27 (analyst-cited ASP growth about 25%).
FY27 capex expected at INR200-300 crore, funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.
FY28 vision: double production capacity versus current levels, complete backward integration in key components, and a fully functional global R&D presence including Taiwan.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity has reached 2.5 million units; management targets 90-100% utilisation.
Housing plant: Phase-1 operational by Q2 FY27 and Phase-2 by Q4 FY27, targeting 30 million housings and enclosures per year.
New lens assembly line commissioning with initial capacity of 5 lakh lenses per month, scalable to 1 million per month; CCTV lens production to start soon at Kadapa.
Kadapa: acquiring additional land and adding a 50,000 sq ft shed. Noida: proposed 3 lakh sq ft facility in Sector 68, operational by Q4 FY27.
Orient Cables JV for LAN and CCTV cable manufacturing: plant in Rajasthan (about 1 lakh sq ft), commercial operations expected between Q2 and Q3 FY27.
HD analog job work planned to move to EMS partners at about 0.5 million units per month. Evaluating further land in North India.
demand_pricing: Price hike of 6-8% taken in January 2026; management now moves prices monthly in small steps (single-digit % per month, varying by category) to avoid shocking customers. Further increases expected in FY27.

Market unit growth expected at 15-16% for FY27. Management says the industry's pent-up demand from the STQC transition was muted in FY26, and ASP increases are heavier on entry-level IP and NVR than on enterprise/project segments.
Consumer purchases are under 10% of the business; the business is largely B2B. Government is 15-20% of revenue and management plans for a similar share.

Competition: about 30 certified brands. A dozen global brands hold about 10% share; about 1.5 dozen domestic brands are each far smaller (about one-tenth of AIL's size or less). Management sees no single clear number-two player.
Memory: half of the 6-7 non-China DDR makers have stopped DDR3 output, pushing supply tightness onto smaller players. Management says scale lets AIL secure supply ahead of competitors.
Volume vs value in FY26: volume growth about 18-20%, with the rest from ASP and mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 gross margin (about 31.8%) came from low-cost inventory, mix or price rise, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair cited a mix of low-cost inventory, the Q4 price rise and higher-end SKUs (STQC-certified project SKUs from H2). He said the low-cost inventory is now mostly used up, but FY27 guidance is above FY26 and slightly below Q4 margin.

qa_highlights.question: Cash conversion cycle and working capital needs with advance chip and memory purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said the cash conversion cycle has risen because creditors fell as the company secured supply, and some inventory is being blocked with advance payments. Working capital is factored into FY27 plans; capex is to be funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said the earlier plan of about INR200 crore has been raised to INR200-300 crore for FY27, with FY28 plans still under work. Funding is through internal accruals and some debt; the debt-equity ratio is very low.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14-15% EBITDA margin the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said 14-15% should be the new normal for FY27 and FY28, driven by localisation, cost optimisation, the shift to higher-end and enterprise products and premiumisation. Q4 was a one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Export plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said export action may start in FY27, but domestic demand comes first. Some thoughts are underway and the outcome is not yet clear.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split FY26: volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said volume growth was about 18-20% and the rest came from ASP and mix. The price rise was mainly in Q4. For FY27, ASP growth is about 25% and volume growth 25-30%.

risks_watch: Chip and memory supply: lead times are long, contracts are being invalidated under force majeure, and management says costs are rising every fortnight to week. Watch whether monthly price increases keep pace.
Margin sustainability: low-cost inventory is used up, and the cash conversion cycle has lengthened due to advance payments and lower creditors.
Demand: entry-level IP and NVR demand may shift to analog as price rises. Consumer and mobile-style demand softness is a risk in the wider market.
Execution: housing plant (Phase-1 Q2 FY27), lens line, Noida facility (Q4 FY27) and Rajasthan cable JV (Q2-Q3 FY27) all need to meet timelines. Doubling capacity by FY28 is a target.

New brands: Nexivue has started shipping since April 2026. Eyra is delayed by R&D rework and may reach market next quarter. Qualcomm AI platform is in trials and commercial rollout is phased. Certification pace is a watch item.
Competition: a more certified competitor base could arrive from 2028 onward, according to the analyst's question. Management says it has a head start on localisation, capacity and supply.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, share and the raised FY27 guidance, but cautious on cost and supply. Management was more guarded on exact margin bridges, the cloud/SaaS monetisation timeline and the B2C/government split, which it deferred to IR.
key_quotes: So, we think the margins are sustainable, but if you see our guidance, we have factored for that, our guidance for the whole year is higher than our last year guidance but slightly lower than the Q4.
So, I would say Naushad, this should be the new normal for this business.
So, it will be a single -digit price rise every month sort of a thing.
